lessons.claim: How the 2026-09-15/16 cross-repository session actually produced findings, stated as a mechanism rather than as credit: a SHAPE crosses between repositories and a SURFACE does not. Each finding was one side handing over a form and the other applying it to a surface the giver could not see. The bridge session enumerated its error-producing rules with no negative fixture and found four; applying the same form here found 88 of 154 error paths never executed. It measured its own warning volume; the same check here found a test that passed vacuously with an empty parameter list. It named rule-versus-branch granularity; the same distinction then appeared twice more here, as exception-type-versus-message and source-line-versus-full-expression. In every case the form was transferable and the finding was not, because neither side could see the other's surface. The operative half is cheap and is the whole contribution: RUN THE OTHER SIDE'S FORM ON YOURSELF IMMEDIATELY, AND EXPECT THE ANSWER TO BE WORSE THAN YOU THINK -- three times out of three it was. Corollary, from the same session: a test that can only ever say 'do more' is a ratchet and not a test; the evidence that a criterion is calibrated is an occasion on which it said no (here, the two-tier correction test declining to spend a round document on a midpoint quoted for a range).
